proposed_comments.title: Make profile application non-destructive and failure-safe
proposed_comments.body:
### Make profile application non-destructive and failure-safe

**Severity:** `high`

The profile path is user state, but the current write goes through an API that swallows I/O exceptions and writes the destination directly. A failed or partial write can therefore damage the existing remappings before the later verification reports failure. Write the complete JSON to a same-directory temporary file and atomically replace the destination only after that succeeds; do not signal a reload until the replacement is complete. Keep reads non-mutating for missing, null, or corrupt settings/profile documents, validate the active configuration before deriving a path, and isolate the tests from the real user settings directory and machine-wide event with an injected filesystem and signal callback.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve engine semantics across profile export and import
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve engine semantics across profile export and import

**Severity:** `high`

The engine decodes both shortcut sections from the same `operationType` and target fields, accepts persisted `ProgramAlreadyRunningAction` value 5, and can load valid chord key orders that canonical formatting changes. Exporting these states as unconditional text, omitting value 5, or reordering the stored source changes behavior when the export is applied. Decode actions independently of the storage section, preserve engine-valid chord meaning, and surface a warning whenever malformed or unsupported stored entries must be skipped. When filtering an invalid export entry, revalidate after each removal so a later valid overlapping remap is not discarded with it; add round-trip tests for cross-section actions, noncanonical chords, `closeAndEndTask`, warning propagation, and overlapping entries.
